Character -> Skills -> Knowledge native source reconstruction

This is an offline decompilation of the configured PE instruction bodies and
immutable selector tables. Symbolic names below describe recovered behavior;
they are not recovered debug symbols. Nothing here is a display observation,
translation execution, test result or build output.

SOURCE ROOTS
  reference Character selection/input owner 0x1aa060..0x1b9a18
  classic   Character selection/input owner 0x1a9ff0..0x1b99a8
  reference Knowledge dispatch 0x1b392c..0x1b413f
  classic corresponding dispatch is retained in classic-1a9ff0.asm
  reference work body 0xcc5d50..0xcc699f, selectors 0xcc69a0..0xcc6a0e
  classic   work body 0xcc2d90..0xcc39df, selectors 0xcc39e0..0xcc3a4e
  reference style body 0xcc5520..0xcc5d07, selector 0xcc5d08
  classic   style body 0xcc2560..0xcc2d47, selector 0xcc2d48
  reference form roots: dance 0x4ea820; music 0xdd5ce0; poetry 0xe76400
  classic   form roots: dance 0x4e83e0; music 0xdd0c50; poetry 0xe71370

functions.tsv gives each complete source extent and its current-image identity.
branches.tsv contains both destinations of every decoded conditional branch.
conditions.tsv retains cmp/test/bt operands. switches.tsv contains every input
selector, optional byte remap, and actual DWORD destination. calls.tsv retains
direct and virtual/indirect calls. literals.tsv retains exact literal operands,
including separator strings, substring loads and inline packed fragments.

KNOWLEDGE SELECTION DISPATCH
  selected entry type is stored separately from selected entry ID.
  Type 14: resolve dance form; absent -> exit without a document; present ->
           [C:7:0:1] + complete dance-form description.
  Type 15: resolve musical form; absent -> exit; present ->
           [C:7:0:1] + complete musical-form description.
  Type 16: resolve poetic form; absent -> exit; present ->
           [C:7:0:1] + complete poetic-form description.
  Type 17: resolve written content; absent -> exit; present -> work document.
  All other values leave this document-building branch without constructing a
  new text. Scholarly topics additionally occur as general_ref subjects below.
  A complete constructed document is assigned to sheet+0x1bc0 and wrapped by
  the existing rich text mechanism; [C:...] and [B] are native markup.

WRITTEN-CONTENT FIELDS
  +0x00 int32 ID
  +0x08 std::string title, length at +0x18
  +0x30 vector<general_ref *> begin; +0x38 end
  +0x48 parallel int32 role vector begin
  +0x68 int32 genre; +0x6c int32 form ID
  +0x70 vector<int32> style begin; +0x78 end
  +0x88 parallel style strength vector begin
  +0xa0 author historical-figure ID
  +0xa4 int32 quality/author roll

DOCUMENT INTRODUCTION
  out = [C:7:0:1]
  if title is nonempty:
      out += title + " is " + article(genre) + " "
  else:
      out += "This is an untitled" + " "
  append genre label only if unsigned(genre) <= 25.
  The article remap uses "an" for genres 6, 10, 17, 20 and 25; every other
  value, including genre outside 0..25, uses "a".
  Genre table, in exact selector order:
   0 manual; 1 guide; 2 chronicle; 3 short story; 4 novel; 5 biography;
   6 autobiography; 7 poem; 8 play; 9 letter; 10 essay; 11 dialog;
   12 musical composition; 13 choreography; 14 comparative biography;
   15 biographical dictionary; 16 genealogy; 17 encyclopedia;
   18 cultural history; 19 cultural comparison; 20 alternate history;
   21 treatise on technological evolution; 22 dictionary; 23 star chart;
   24 star catalogue; 25 atlas.
  Native article behavior is preserved as source; it follows the extracted
  remap rather than guessed spelling rules.
  If author != -1 and the figure lookup succeeds:
      append ", authored by "; resolve current/original figure identity;
      append its formatted name only when the name record exists and has a name.
  A successful author lookup with an absent name still leaves the entire
  authored-by prefix in the native text. A missing author emits no prefix.
  Always append ".  ". Therefore defaults can emit:
      TITLE is a .
      This is an untitled .
      TITLE is a , authored by NAME.
      This is an untitled , authored by .
  For genre 7/12/13, resolve poetic/musical/dance form by +0x6c:
      If absent: append work_body(work, mode=0) only.
      If present: append "It is an example of " + generated form name + ".  ";
          append work_body(work,0) + "[B]" + complete corresponding form body.
  Form record existence does not imply a nonempty generated name. The formatter
  a946e0 tests name+0x72 has_name at 0xa94723/0xa94727 and directly returns via
  0xa94e6f when false. The caller has initialized its name string to empty, so
  this branch produces "It is an example of .  ". The form body itself also
  calls this formatter and can start with its literal " is"/" is a " after an
  empty name. No implicit The/the prefix is appended before this early return.
  None of the three form body roots checks has_name before constructing text:
    dance: generated name + " is a " + usage/solo/group qualifiers + " dance";
      reference fixed fragments at 0x4ea895 and 0x4ea9da. An unknown usage
      selector leaves qualifiers empty, giving " is a  dance" before later
      dancer-count/origin/deity/music/poetry clauses.
    music: generated name + " is a " (0xdd5d50) + usage phrase:
      0 "form of music used for entertainment";
      1 "form of music used to commemorate important events";
      2 "devotional form of music" (+ optional worship clause);
      3 "form of music used during marches and military engagements";
      default emits no usage phrase. Origin/creator fields and ".  " still
      follow, so the anonymous default can produce " is a .  ".
    poetry: generated name + " is" (0xe76478) + type adjective phrase:
      1 " a dramatic"; 2 " a reflective"; 4 " a ribald"; 5 " a light";
      6 " a solemn"; default/0/3 " a";
      then " poetic " (0xe764e9) + 0 "narrative" / 3 "riddle" /
      every other value "form". Topic/intent/origin/structure clauses follow.
  Empty names therefore reach existing anonymous grammar after leading-space
  normalization: "is a ... dance", "is a ... form of music", and
  "is a [adjective] poetic form/narrative/riddle". The name field's absence
  must not reject the entire document or drop its following form paragraphs.
  Every other genre, including default, appends work_body(work,0) only.

WORK BODY (reference 0xcc5d50; classic 0xcc2d90)
  subject_count = count(role == 0)
  chapter_count = count(role == 5)
  All reference counts include references whose description is empty.
  if subject_count == 0:
      append "The work has no particular subject.  "
  else if subject_count == 1 and genre == 20:
      append 'It asks the question, "What if '
      append reference_description(first role-0 ref, mode)
      append ' had unfolded differently?"  '
  else if subject_count == 1 and genre == 16:
      append "It concerns the lineage of " + ref + ".  "
  else:
      append "It concerns "
      for every role-0 ref in source order:
          append its virtual +0x90 description, even if empty
          decrement remaining subject count
          if remaining >= 2: append ", "
          else if remaining == 1: append " and "
          else: append ".  "
  An empty reference is not the no-subject branch. It can produce "It concerns
  .  ", "It concerns  and SUBJECT.  ", "It concerns SUBJECT and .  ", or an
  empty field in a longer comma list. Genre 16 and 20 preserve their entire
  specialized sentence with an empty field too.

  Scan all references in native vector order again:
      role 6: "The writing conveys a moral lesson regarding " + ref + ".  "
      role 9: "The overall text emphasizes " + ref + ".  "
      role 7: "For lyrics, the composer has selected " + ref + ".  "
      role 8: "For musical accompaniment, the choreographer has selected "
                  + ref + ".  "
      Other roles emit no sentence in this pass.
  The same empty descriptions are possible in all four role sentences.

  If style_count != 0:
      append "The writing " + style(style[0],strength[0],quality)
      If style_count >= 2:
          neg(s) = s in {2,13,15} or
                   (s in {0,3,5,6,8,9,10,17} and quality < 20)
          append " and it " if neg(first)==neg(second), else " yet it "
          append style(style[1],strength[1],quality)
      append ".  "
  Only the first two styles are used even when the stored vector is longer.
  The style helper emits nothing for selector outside 0..17 or strength outside
  0..2; its default return preserves the sentence's empty style position.
  style-productions.tsv reconstructs all actual style/strength/quality branches
  from the extracted instructions and immutable table, including native paths.
  There are 18 styles with three strengths. Eight switch all three predicates
  at quality 20; the other ten retain the same three predicates.

  Quality family selector for genres 0..25:
      [0,0,1,0,0,0,0,2,0,0,0,0,3,4,0,0,1,0,0,0,0,0,1,1,1,1]
  Genre outside 0..25 uses family 0 (prose).
  Family 0 prose; 1 compiled information; 2 poetry; 3 composition;
         4 choreography.
  Quality bands, in order: q<10, 10<=q<20, 20<=q<30, 30<=q<40,
                          40<=q<50, q>=50.
  One full quality statement is always appended, then ".  ". All thirty exact
  native statements, including "Overall, the splendid source of information",
  are literal operands in the retained body and literals.tsv.

  if chapter_count == 1: append "The work has a single chapter.  "
  if chapter_count >= 2:
      append "The work has " + number_as_words(chapter_count) + " chapters.  "
  Then each role-5 reference, in source order:
      if chapter_count == 1: append "It"
      else: append "The " + lowercase(ordinal_as_words(index+1)) + " chapter"
      append " covers " + ref + ".  "
  Empty chapter descriptions still keep "It covers ." or the ordinal chapter
  sentence. The cardinal/ordinal helpers are dynamic numeric fields, not
  a fixed list of chapter counts.

REFERENCE DESCRIPTION DISPATCH
  Every reference's actual vtable +0x90 is discovered from the current PE RTTI;
  reference-bindings.tsv preserves all classes, including shared base methods.
  Complete unique supplier bodies are retained rather than guessed from names.
  Fields below describe actual output sources and empty/default alternatives:

  general_refst: clears result to empty, emits no label (all inherited classes).
  poetic/musical/dance form: resolve form ID, format generated form name;
      add " as a poetic form" / " as a musical form" / " as a dance form".
      Missing records return empty.
  written content: resolve work ID and copy its stored title. If its first four
      bytes are "The ", lowercase only the initial T. Missing or empty title
      returns empty. The title is stored data, not a list of literal book names.
  language: "the " + lowercased/normalized language RAW name + " language".
  value level: level<-10 -> "the worthlessness of "; level>10 -> "the value
      of "; otherwise "nuances of ". Append one of 33 value labels if the
      unsigned selector is <=32; unknown selectors leave the trailing " of ".
  knowledge scholar flag: category 0..13 and exact one-bit flag select a topic;
      unknown category/flag returns empty. scholar-productions.tsv contains
      every category and 32 flag positions, including native empty defaults.
      This +0x90 vocabulary differs from history-event discourse names; e.g.
      category0 flag0x80 is "medical ethics", flag0x100 is "the meaning of
      individual happiness". Do not substitute event-specific labels.
  interaction: requires both IDs != -1 and interaction source type == 1;
      copy that source's +0x10 NAME. Any rejected branch returns empty.
  artifact: lookup artifact; absent -> "an unknown artifact". Present ->
      article/item noun and named artifact identity according to native flags.
  abstract building: typed building label (including dungeon/sewer/catacomb
      subtypes) and generated building name; unknown label/name fields can be
      empty while native surrounding "the " and " " remain.
  historical event: resolve event; missing -> empty; present -> actual
      history_event vtable +0xd8 description, mode passed through.
  historical figure/site: native type/caste/site label and optional generated
      name, with the native prefix and separation preserved.
  sphere: native sphere selector helper; unknown sphere -> empty.
  subregion: resolve region and generated name; missing/name absent -> empty.
  feature layer: generated name if named; otherwise depth type0 "the depths
      of the world", type1 "the fiery bowels of the earth", type2 "the
      Underworld"; unknown type -> empty.
  entity population: creature RAW descriptor; independently apply animated
      corpse and ghost flags; prefix "a population of ".
  creature: creature RAW descriptor; independently apply animated corpse and
      ghost flags; singular branches retain native article wording.
  item type: "a " + shared item noun derived from type/subtype/material tuple.
  entity: generated entity name if named, otherwise "an unnamed group".

POETIC PURPOSE AND TOPIC SOURCE GRAMMAR
  The following is reconstructed from the saved complete form bodies plus a
  read of the current two PE topic suppliers. Addresses below are RVAs, not
  observations of a running game. Topic supplier: reference 0xe76080 with
  instructions through 0xe763a5 and selector table at 0xe763a8; classic
  0xe70ff0 with instructions through 0xe71315 and table at 0xe71318.

  topic(out, kind, target):
      if unsigned(kind) > 20: return without appending anything
      kind 0:  append "the past"
           1:  append "current events"
           2:  append "the future"
           3:  append "someone recently deceased"
           4:  append "someone recently retired"
           5:  append "religion"
           6:  append "a specific place"
           7:  append "a specific wilderness region"
           8:  append "nature"
           9:  append "a lover"
          10:  append "family"
          11:  append "alcoholic beverages"
          12:  append "a journey"
          13:  append "war"
          14:  append "the hunt"
          15:  append "mining"
          16:  append "death"
          17:  append "immortality"
          18:  append "someone's character"
          19:  if target == -1: append "a historical figure"
               else call historical-figure formatter directly into out
          20:  if target == -1: append "an abstract concept"
               else if target == 21: append "the concept of death"
               else if target == 30: append "the concept of family"
               else if target == 48: append "the concept of hunting"
               else if target == 75: append "the concept of nature"
               else if target == 122: append "the concept of war"
               else:
                   temp = empty string
                   sphere(uint16(target), temp)
                   append temp directly into out
  Reference concept comparisons start at 0xe76128; the five complete concept
  literals are at producer instructions 0xe7625f/0xe7624d/0xe7623b/0xe76229/
  0xe76217. The generic branch narrows target at 0xe76194, calls sphere
  0x756690 at 0xe76198, and appends its result at 0xe761c2. Classic performs
  the identical comparisons and calls sphere 0x7540b0 at 0xe71108.
  There is no generic "the concept of " append. An unknown sphere can leave
  this whole topic empty, but cannot leave that prefix behind. The five
  special concepts are complete literals rather than prefix plus dynamic
  field. Unknown kind and a dynamic figure formatter with no output can
  likewise leave the whole topic empty.

  Action selectors and flags:
      selector     exact action literal                    absent-topic flag
       0           "to describe"                           chosen subject
       1           "to satirize"                           chosen subject
       2           "to amuse the audience"                 concerning
       3           "to complain about"                     chosen subject
       4           "to renounce"                           none
       5           "to make an apology"                    concerning
       6           "to express pleasure with"              chosen subject
       7           "to express grief over"                 chosen subject
       8           "to praise"                             chosen subject
       9           "to teach a moral lesson"                concerning
      10           "to make an assertion"                  concerning
      11           "to make a counter-assertion"            concerning
      12           "to make a concession"                  concerning
      13           "to synthesize previous ideas"           concerning
      14           "to develop the previous idea"           concerning
      15           "to invert the previous assertion"       concerning
      16           "to undercut the previous assertion"     concerning
      17           "to move away from previous ideas"       concerning
      18           "to reflect on previous ideas"           concerning
      19           "to console the audience"                concerning
      20           "to refuse consolation"                  concerning
      21           "to offer a different perspective"       concerning
      22           "to beseech"                             none
  The chosen-subject flag supplies a placeholder only when kind == -1. The
  concerning flag supplies " concerning" only when kind != -1; it does not
  validate whether the topic helper will append a nonempty result.
  Root introduction has no action for selectors 11, 13..18 and 21. Their
  switch entries all point straight to 0xe76666 / classic 0xe715d6 with both
  flags zero, exactly like unsigned purpose > 22. Parts and lines have all
  23 action entries, except the output destination caveat below. All three
  locations treat purpose == -1 separately; every other negative purpose
  takes the unsigned default branch.

  Form root fields: +0xd0 mood, +0xd4 kind, +0xd8 target, +0xdc purpose.
  Its already-appended name/type text is followed by:
      if purpose != -1:
          append " intended "                 [0xe7654a / 0xe714ba]
          append action if the root switch has one; set its flags
          if kind != -1:
              if concerning flag: append " concerning"
              append " "
              topic(out, kind, target)          [0xe766a6 / 0xe71616]
          else if chosen-subject flag:
              append " a chosen subject"
      else if kind != -1:
          append " concerning "               [0xe76736 / 0xe716a6]
          topic(out, kind, target)
      append origin/creator clause if selected, then ".  "
  Therefore default purpose with a nonempty topic emits " intended  TOPIC"
  before space normalization, or " intended TOPIC" afterward. It does not
  introduce "concerning". Default purpose with absent/empty topic leaves
  " intended "; purpose -1 with an empty topic leaves " concerning ". A
  valid concerning action plus an empty helper result leaves its action and
  " concerning ". Default/no-output action is not the purpose -1 branch.

  Part fields on each section record: +0x180 mood, +0x184 kind,
  +0x188 target, +0x18c purpose. Line values come from section vectors
  +0xe0 mood, +0xf8 kind, +0x110 target and +0x128 purpose. Missing mood,
  kind and purpose elements are initialized to -1; target is read together
  with a present kind element. The part and line text independently select
  actions but call the identical topic helper used by the introduction:
      part call 0xe78fd9 / classic 0xe73f49
      line call 0xe7a9f0 / classic 0xe75960
  They are not work general_ref descriptions and do not use a separate
  "concept of" prefix generator.

  part_or_line_predicate(out, mood, purpose, kind, target):
      append subject + " "
      append mood predicate only if unsigned(mood) <= 6:
          0 "is a narrative"; 1 "is dramatic"; 2 "is reflective";
          3 "is a riddle"; 4 "is ribald"; 5 "is light"; 6 "is solemn"
      if purpose != -1:
          append "is" if mood == -1, otherwise " and"
          append " intended "
          append selected action and set flags (default leaves flags zero)
          if kind != -1:
              if concerning flag: append " concerning"
              append " "; topic(out, kind, target)
          else if chosen-subject flag:
              append " the subject of the poem"
      else if kind != -1:
          if mood != -1: append " and "
          append "concerns "; topic(out, kind, target)
      append ".  "
  Native part subjects are "It" for a single part, or "The " plus the
  lowercase ordinal and " part" for multiple parts. Line subjects are "The "
  plus lowercase ordinal and " line". The ordinal is generated dynamically.
  The part gate skips this predicate only when all of mood/purpose/kind are
  exactly -1 (0xe78c92..0xe78cae). The line gate instead tests whether any of
  the three vectors mood/kind/purpose is nonempty (0xe7a5fd..0xe7a634). It
  does not skip a current index whose three values are all missing or -1.
  That path still emits "The ORDINAL line .  ".

  Source prefixes, reference / classic:
      part " intended " 0xe78dce / 0xe73d3e
      part "concerns "  0xe78fb7 / 0xe73f27
      line " intended " 0xe7a7ef / 0xe7575f
      line "concerns "  0xe7a9d6 / 0xe75946
  Each precedes the helper's possible empty return. With mood -1 these paths
  really produce "It is intended .  ", "It concerns .  ", and corresponding
  ordinal part/line clauses. Trimming/normalizing the gap before punctuation
  yields "It is intended.", "It concerns.", "The first part is intended.",
  "The first part concerns.", "The first line is intended." or "The first
  line concerns.". These are native empty/default productions, not missing
  literals inferred from a screenshot.
  Unknown mood != -1 emits no mood predicate but still chooses the " and"
  or " and " path. It can leave "It  and intended .  " or "The first line
   and concerns .  " before space normalization.
  Complete normalized unknown-mood combinations (S is the actual It/part/line
  subject; T is the topic helper result, possibly empty):
      purpose == -1, kind == -1:
          S.
          No "is" is appended. "It is." is not this native branch.
      purpose == -1, kind != -1:
          S and concerns T.       [empty T: S and concerns.]
      default purpose != -1, kind == -1 or empty T:
          S and intended.
      default purpose != -1, kind != -1, nonempty T:
          S and intended T.
      chosen-subject action, kind == -1:
          S and intended ACTION the subject of the poem.
      chosen-subject action, kind != -1:
          S and intended ACTION T. [empty T: S and intended ACTION.]
      concerning action, kind == -1:
          S and intended ACTION.
      concerning action, kind != -1:
          S and intended ACTION concerning T.
          [empty T: S and intended ACTION concerning.]
      purpose 4, kind == -1 or empty T:
          S and intended to renounce.
      purpose 4, kind != -1, nonempty T:
          S and intended to renounce T.
  Part/line purpose 22 has the local default shape for every mood, with its
  out-of-paragraph literal append described below. A part with exactly -1
  mood/purpose/kind emits no predicate at all; an unknown non--1 mood and
  absent purpose/kind emits "It.", or "The ORDINAL part.". The independent
  line-vector gate permits "The ORDINAL line." even when all three current
  values are exactly -1, provided one of those vectors is nonempty elsewhere.

  Output destination caveat retained from both image bodies: part purpose 22
  appends "to beseech" at 0xe78ece / 0xe73e3e with rcx=r12, the complete
  document string; line purpose 22 at 0xe7a8ec / 0xe7585c uses rcx=rbx,
  likewise the document pointer loaded at 0xe7a5e4 / 0xe75554. Other part/line
  actions append into local paragraph [rbp+0x28]. Thus this literal reaches
  the complete document outside its local intended clause. The local clause
  retains the no-action shape, including an empty "is intended" suffix.
  Its precise output order is immediate global += "to beseech" (with no
  leading/trailing space), then continued construction of the local section
  paragraph. Only at 0xe7c7c6..0xe7c7fa / classic 0xe77736..0xe7776a does
  the completed nonempty paragraph reach global. If the form has at least
  two sections, this final append first adds "[B]"; a single section adds
  no separator. Thus source text can contain:
      single section, part purpose22:
          ... .  to beseechIt is intended .  OTHER_LOCAL_SENTENCES
      single section, no part predicate, first local sentence is line:
          ... .  to beseechThe first line is intended .  ...
      two or more sections, first part purpose22:
          ... .  to beseech[B]The first part is intended .  ...
  After ordinary whitespace/punctuation normalization these retain adjacent
  "to beseechIt" or "to beseechThe"; native inserted no space to split them.
  The markup variant retains "to beseech[B]The". Part purpose22 followed by
  N line-purpose22 cases in that same section appends N+1 literal copies to
  global before the paragraph: "to beseechto beseech...", then optional [B],
  then the entire local paragraph in its original order. Local prefix text
  need not be the corresponding line: previous part/property sentences also
  remain inside that delayed paragraph. This is a prefix-before-paragraph
  production, not a trailing action after the intended sentence.

DOWNSTREAM SOURCE OWNERSHIP
  Whole form bodies are in this directory, including all their predicates,
  section/role/group/music/dance/poetry literal operands and selector tables.
  The existing complementary complete semantic reconstruction is
  data/extracted/adventure-performance-menu/steam-decompiled.txt; its helper
  bodies use the identical reference form entries listed above.
  Shared generated name formatting: a946e0 (reference); name fields remain
  world data, including native WORD forms and authored names.
  Shared item noun branch graph and typed RAW fields:
  data/extracted/item-description-sources.tsv, shared-item-noun 0xa82c10.
  Historical-event virtual +0xd8 RTTI roots and transitive text suppliers:
  data/extracted/statue-history-sources.tsv and artwork-history-native source
  graph. These catalogs own all historical-event subject wording.
  Exact runtime reference-kind/creature/material/name values cannot be a closed
  list of English literals: mods and saved world objects can author them.
  Translation must retain the typed dynamic field path and empty alternatives,
  rather than inventing a finite list of every possible world-generated name.
